artifacts.summary: Confirms the eager-load budget breach (67,003 B vs 65,950 B baseline), attributes it entirely to task 227's rewrite of the source-store rule's 'Correct Edit Target' section, and specifies a byte-measured rule/lazy-narrative split (rule trimmed to 1,496 B, new context/standards/source-store-deploy-boundary-narrative.md at 3,921 B) projected to land at 64,056 B TOTAL with 1,894 B headroom.

memory_candidates.content: This codebase's rule-file byte-budget pattern: when an eagerly-loaded rules/X.md grows past its budget, split it into a small eager core (path pattern, principle, one-line pointer) plus a lazily-loaded context/standards/X-narrative.md companion, referenced only via a plain backticked path (never @-import, which would re-eager it). Two existing precedents: rules/git-workflow.md -> context/standards/git-workflow-narrative.md, rules/state-management.md -> context/reference/state-management-schema.md.

agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/measure-eager-context.sh --check sums four channels (parent_chain, claudemd predicted-assembled, at_import, rules) into a TOTAL compared against context/config/orchestrator-context-budget.json's eager_load.baseline_bytes by verify-deploy.sh gate 20. A rules/*.md file counts as eager only when it lacks a paths: frontmatter gate. Completing a task that edits such a file without re-running this check can silently breach the budget (as task 227 did, growing rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md 62% with the budget gate never run).
